chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was seated in the study-circle of Rabia al-Rayy, when a bedouin came and asked Rabia al-Rayy about a matter, and he answered him. When he was silent, the bedouin said to him: 'Is it upon your neck?' Rabia remained silent and did not reply to him. He repeated the question to him, and he answered in the same way. The bedouin said to him again: 'Is it upon your neck?' Rabia remained silent. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'It is upon his neck.' He said: 'Did he not say: And every giver of Fatwa is liable?'

key_terms.أَعْرَابِيٌّ: Bedouin, often used in hadith to denote someone from the desert or simple in manner
key_terms.حَلْقَة: Study-circle or gathering for learning and teaching
key_terms.رَبِيعَ الرَّأْيِ: Rabia al-Rayy, a prominent early jurist known for his reliance on personal opinion (Ra'y)
key_terms.فِي عُنُقِهِ: Upon his neck, an idiom meaning 'upon his responsibility' or 'liable'
key_terms.مُفْتٍ: Jurist or one who issues a Fatwa (legal opinion)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a jurist's responsibility when giving a Fatwa if they remain silent about liability?
ai.summary: This incident highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the accountability (daman) of jurists who issue fatwas based on personal opinion (ra'y) rather than definitive evidence, as seen in the contrast between Rabia al-Rayy and the Ahl al-Bayt. The Imam’s clarification underscores that silence does not absolve one of the spiritual and legal burden of one's rulings, reinforcing the principle that every mujtahid is responsible for the accuracy of his deduction. This narrative serves as a critical warning against casual legal reasoning in early Islamic jurisprudence.

en.ammaar-muslim: 7. [7/41] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman b. al-Hajjaj who said:

Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was seated in a study-circle of Rabia al-Rayy when a bedouin came and asked Rabia al-Rayy about a matter and he (Rabia) proceeded to answer him, so when he was done (answering) the bedouin asked: is it upon your neck (do you accept responsibility for me following your answer)? Rabia remained silent and did not say anything, so he (the bedouin) repeated the question again and he (Rabia) answered in the same way, so the bedouin said to him again: is it upon your neck? but Rabia remained silent, then Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said to him: it is upon his neck whether he declares it to be so or not, and every giver of Fatwa is liable.
